generation.hypothesis: High-throughput computational screening and mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering can be used for phase stability, microstructure refinement, and property optimization in high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy in its initial, unprocessed state
generation.intervention: High-throughput computational screening and mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering
generation.conditions: Varied processing conditions such as temperature, pressure, and composition
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of precipitates, grain refinement, and solid solution strengthening
generation.mechanism: The combination of computational screening for optimal composition and mechanical alloying with spark plasma sintering leads to refined microstructures and enhanced properties due to solid solution strengthening, grain boundary strengthening, and precipitation strengthening.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved yield strength, fracture strength, and high-temperature stability in high-entropy alloys
generation.baseline: Traditional casting and processing methods for high-entropy alloys
generation.boundary: Limitations in current thermodynamic databases and potential issues with ductility and fracture mechanisms

Question: How does the combination of mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering affect the microstructure evolution and mechanical properties of an equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy, particularly regarding the formation of secondary phases due to interstitial elements?. System: Equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy (Nb: 16.67 at%, Mo: 16.67 at%, Ta: 16.67 at%, W: 16.67 at%, V: 16.67 at%, Ti: 16.67 at%) with oxygen introduction. Processing: Mechanical alloying of elemental powders (≥99.9% purity) in a high energy planetary ball mill with stainless steel balls/vial at a ball-to-powder weight ratio of 13:1 under high purity argon for 40 h; followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) of the 40 h milled powders in a graphite die at 1400 °C for 10 min under 30 MPa pressure, with a heating rate of 100 °C/min and cooling to 500 °C at 300 °C/min. Question: How can high-throughput computational screening be used to discover lightweight, precipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloys with high-temperature strength superior to traditional ferritic superalloys?. System: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system (specifically Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5 and Al15Cr5Fe50Mn25Ti5 as successful cases). Processing: Arc-melting of 99.9 wt% purity constituent elements, melted at least six times for homogeneity, followed by drop-casting; subsequent homogenization at 1200 °C and annealing at 700 °C for 2 hours for specific characterizations. Test conditions: Compression tests at room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 700 °C) at a strain rate of 2 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; in situ neutron scattering from room temperature to 1050 °C; synchrotron XRD and TEM characterization.
